gap: No result ChatGPT got turns idle or access wattage into a yearly electricity bill. At the August 2026 U.S. average of 18.19¢/kWh (EIA, year to date), one watt running all year costs $1.59. That puts the DS925+ at about $60/yr at Synology's access figure, the QNAP TS-464 at about $65/yr at QNAP's operating figure, and the UGREEN DXP4800 Plus at about $39/yr idle on 2.5GbE as KitGuru measured it. Over five years, the extra cost of running the QNAP instead of the UGREEN is about $130.
standout_why: Starry Hope's Best 4-Bay NAS page (cited in two chats) already gives wattage: UGREEN DXP4800 Plus about 24 W idle (KitGuru), DS925+ about 730 Wh/day (Dong Knows Tech) and F4-425 Plus 13 W with SSDs only. It does not give annual cost or total cost of ownership. QNAP's own spec pages (cited in one chat) give 21.6 W disk standby and 40.5 W operating but no cost. So rivals already have the inputs, and our page would add only the dollar conversion and the side-by-side. The gaps are $5–25 a year, too small to change the pick.
decides: This confirms the pick rather than changing it. The DXP4800 Plus ($619.99 on UGREEN's US store today) also has the lowest running cost of the candidates I could source: about $39/yr idle on 2.5GbE, and about $49/yr idle on 10GbE. The QNAP TS-464, the 'mature software' alternative, comes to about $65/yr at its rated operating draw. Its bill also stays higher with disks asleep: $34/yr at 21.6 W standby, against $20/yr for the DS925+ at 12.3 W hibernation and $10/yr for the DS425+ at 6.1 W. A shopper whose NAS sits idle with disks spun down most of the day should see Synology as the cheapest to run, not the most expensive. Note that the UGREEN figure is a reviewer's idle measurement while the QNAP and Synology figures are maker ratings, so the comparison is directional, not like-for-like.

unsourced: TerraMaster F4-425 Plus rated power and warranty: terra-master.com returned HTTP 429 on all three tries. The only reviewer figure I have is NASCompares' 13 W idle with SSDs and no HDDs, reported second-hand by Starry Hope, which isn't comparable to the 4-HDD figures.

Asustor Lockerstor 4 Gen2+ (AS6704T v2) power: the asustor.com datasheet PDF came back as unreadable binary, and the local pdftotext extraction step was blocked by a permission prompt. The Gadgeteer and NASCompares v2 reviews give no wattage. Third-party listings quoting 35 W / 17.3 W refer to the original Gen2, so I left them out.

Today's prices for QNAP TS-464, Synology DS925+/DS425+ and Asustor AS6704T v2: none of these makers has a Shopify store, and I didn't run amzcheck within the call budget. Without those prices there is no five-year cost for those models.

UGREEN's own rated power figure for the DXP4800 Plus: the product page returned HTTP 429 and the storecheck product call also hit a 429. The UGREEN running cost therefore rests on KitGuru's measurement, not a maker rating.
